subject: Customer-facing incident brief and action plan — 2026-06-15 service disruption
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-corp.com>, ACME Platform Ops <ops@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Incident summary and customer-facing RCA — 2026-06-15 service disruption

Maria / ACME ops team,

Thank you again for your patience this morning. Attached is a concise customer-facing RCA and a prioritized action plan we will execute with you over the next 30 days. Highlights up front:

- What happened: A regression in our autoscaling router caused a subset of requests to be routed to a legacy GPU pool running an incompatible kernel build, which produced elevated token latencies and intermittent 502s for requests with long contexts.
- Impact window: 2026-06-15T08:47:00Z — 2026-06-15T09:05:00Z (approx. 18 minutes).
- Scope: ~4% of your production requests during the window; no customer data exfiltration or unauthorized access detected.
- Root cause: configuration rollback during a deploy that incorrectly marked a legacy pool as compatible for the new compilation pipeline.

What we include in the attached package (PDF + supporting log extract):
- One-page executive summary and timeline.
- Technical root cause analysis with kernel selection trace.
- Per-customer impact summary (request counts, failed request ids).
- Immediate mitigations applied and permanent fixes planned.

Action items (owner / ETA):
1) Immediate: Pin ACME service route to the verified kernel build (Redwood) — owner: operations infra — completed at 09:04 PT.
2) 72 hours: Deploy a safety guard in the router to block legacy pool assignment for new compilation graphs — owner: runtime team (Marissa) — target: 2026-06-18.
3) 7 days: Automated deploy-verification surfaced in your console project and a formal canary gating mechanism — owner: platform team (Lauren) — target: 2026-06-22.
4) 30 days: Post-deploy audit and confirmation call with your team to validate telemetry and confirm SLA metrics — owner: account team (Jonas) — scheduled slot provided below.

Attachments: Redwood_ACME_RCA_20260615.pdf (PDF, ~130KB); request_logs_excerpt.log (text, ~45KB).

Next steps I propose:
- We can host a 30-minute technical walkthrough for your SREs today at 4pm PT or tomorrow morning — please let me know which works.
- If desired, we will redact and share a CSV of impacted request IDs for your ingestion into internal tooling.

Apologies again for the disruption — we know every minute of degraded inference at scale matters to you. We’ve prioritized both the short-term guardrails and the longer-term changes to prevent recurrence.

Best,

Jonas Weber
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0109
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Redwood_ACME_RCA_20260615.pdf (PDF)]
[Attachment: request_logs_excerpt.log (text)]

From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@acme-corp.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: ACME Platform Ops <ops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 10:31:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident summary and customer-facing RCA — 2026-06-15 service disruption

Jonas,

Thanks for the swift summary and the attachments — I appreciate the timeline. A few quick questions from our side after an initial pass:

1) Can you confirm whether any requests that failed were retried with different backends or dropped entirely? We need to reconcile this with our client-side metrics.
2) The PDF mentions "no customer data exfiltration detected" — can you point me to the specific audit log entries you reviewed or share the query you ran so our security team can cross-check?
3) For the 30-day audit call: please propose two time windows (preferably earlier in the week).

Also our ops engineer (cc'd) asked if you can provide a short excerpt of the KVS cache behavior for requests that timed out — a few example request ids would suffice.

Thanks,
Maria
Director, Platform Engineering | Acme Corp
maria.gomez@acme-corp.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:05:10 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Incident summary and customer-facing RCA — 2026-06-15 service disruption

Team — forwarding Acme's follow-up questions. Please see inline notes below and help me compile the additional artifacts they requested.

Lauren — can you export the audit query (timestamp range 2026-06-15T08:40Z to 2026-06-15T09:10Z) showing auth checks and config change events? They want the raw query to run against their security tools.

Marissa — can you extract 5 example request ids (successful retry vs dropped) and a short KVS cache timeline snippet for each? Keep PII redacted. We will attach these as request_logs_excerpt.log.

I will propose two times for the 30-day audit call after we have the artifacts. Let's target Wednesday 2026-06-17 09:00 PT or Thursday 2026-06-18 11:00 PT as options (we'll confirm availability).

Thanks — Jonas

Subject: Re: Incident summary and customer-facing RCA — 2026-06-15 service disruption

Maria — quick update and the artifacts you requested are attached. Short answers to your Qs: 

1) Retry behavior: Our router retried ~62% of the affected requests to the verified pool and those succeeded. The remaining ~38% were dropped due to upstream connection resets; we include a CSV in the logs showing request_id, status, retry_count.
2) Audit logs: Lauren attached the exact query and a redacted export of the auth/config events for the window. The query looks for config.change events where pool_assignment != previous_assignment in the 08:40–09:10Z window; we also included a timestamped diff blob.
3) KVS cache excerpts and example request ids are in request_logs_excerpt.log. We redacted client IPs and user identifiers per our standard sharing policy.

Proposed 30-day audit call (pick one):
- Wednesday, 2026-06-17 @ 09:00 PT
- Thursday, 2026-06-18 @ 11:00 PT

If either works for your SREs, I will send a calendar invite and include the runbook snippet we'll follow during the call.

Attachments in this message: Redwood_ACME_RCA_20260615.pdf; request_logs_excerpt.log; acme_audit_query.sql (redacted).

Thanks again for partnering closely here — if you want a live zoom now I can pull Marissa in for the kernel-selection trace review.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0109
